## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle math loop (loop1) combined with a mask-based host-scan respawn (loop2) can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈949) falls below the smallest measured N=10000, so it is not directly observable. The L2 spill (N≈60787) sits between N=10000 and N=100000. At death_q=0.01, ns/p FALLS from 8.463 (N=10000) to 7.928 (N=100000) through the L2→DRAM transition, then continues falling to 7.532 (N=10M) — no knee, just overhead amortization as fixed per-call costs dilute. At death_q=0.5 the curve is FLAT at 12.07–12.29 ns/p across all N, confirming death rate raises the floor without altering the N-shape. The absence of any spill knee means the algo is not memory-latency-limited at any working-set size.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.16 GB/s at N=10M, death_q=0.01 — only 30.6% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. At death_q=0.5 bandwidth collapses to 5.61 GB/s (18.8% of ceiling). The algo is compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: the profile at N=10M, death_q=0.01 shows 66.5% compute and only 28.3% backend stall. The transition is driven by death rate, not N — as q rises from 0.01 to 0.5, branch_flush climbs from 2.5% to 20.1% and bandwidth falls from 9.16 to 5.61 GB/s. The algo never approaches the streaming ceiling in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within a single particle, not across particles. `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` operate on four float lanes of one particle's position/velocity, with `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` and `mov.s v3[3], v0[0]` rearranging components. A gather is present: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` performs an indexed single-element load. The per-particle stride is 0x44 (68 bytes), so each iteration touches one particle — explaining why bandwidth stays at 31% of ceiling: there is no cross-particle SIMD to amortize memory traffic. The mask-scan respawn loop is entirely scalar: 45 `ldrb`, 35 `cbz`, and 35 `bl` calls to `_spawn`, processing mask bytes one at a time. Only 9 of 539 instructions are vector-suffixed.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 9.16 GB/s (30.6% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) at death_q=0.01, N=10M, because the compiler's component-wise vectorization (`fmul.4s` within one particle, stride 0x44) cannot stream across particles, and the scalar mask-scan loop (35 `bl`/35 `cbz`/45 `ldrb`) pushes branch_flush to 20.3% at death_q=0.5, dropping bandwidth to 5.61 GB/s. The hypothesis that autovec plus mask-scan approaches the streaming ceiling fails even in the lowest-churn regime.
